title: Money that grows on its growth
summary: With compounding, the growth itself starts to grow, so time matters as much as the amount.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Say ₹1,000 grows by 10% a year (an assumption for this example, not a promise). After one year it is ₹1,100. In the second year the 10% is on ₹1,100, so it becomes ₹1,210. The growth is now growing too. That is **compounding**.

The longer money compounds, the faster it grows, so starting early can matter more than starting big. The rate matters too, but higher rates usually come with more risk. Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: ₹1,000 grows 10% a year, compounded. How much after two years?
Asha and Bilal save the same amount at the same rate. Asha starts five years earlier. Who likely ends up with more?
questions.explanation: Asha's money has more years to grow on its growth.

questions.prompt: Which two things most change how much compounding adds?

options.text: The rate and how long the money stays
The colour of the passbook and the bank's name
The day of the week you start

questions.explanation: Rate and time drive compounding; any rate shown is an assumption, not a promise.
